by_judge.judge: D K SINGH & K. V. ARAVIND
S SUNIL DUTT YADAV & HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR

narrative:
On September 11, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,544 cases across 68 judges and heard 1,293 matters, achieving an overall hearing rate of 50.8%. This represents a significant rebound from the 38.6% rate recorded on September 10 (1,354 heard of 3,509 scheduled) and aligns closely with the 51.4% clearance observed on September 8, driven by reduced docket congestion and improved conversion across core registries.

Individual bench output diverged markedly across court halls. Justice C.M. Poonacha in Hall 31 handled the largest single workload, hearing 141 of 218 scheduled matters (64.7%). High throughput was also recorded by Justice E.S. Indiresh in Hall 18, who heard 68 of 77 cases (88.3%), and Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde in Hall 26, who heard 73 of 99 cases (73.7%). Conversely, Hall 22 experienced complete non-conversion, with zero of 72 scheduled cases taken up across two cause lists, while Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad heard only 9 of 123 matters (7.3%) on his primary Hall 7 roster.

By procedural stage, earlier-phase matters drove court activity. Admission stages achieved a 57.9% hearing rate (453 heard of 782 scheduled), up from 46.5% on September 10, while Orders converted at 50.6% (411 of 812), compared to 40.5% the previous day. Final Hearing matters remained subdued at 30.5% (113 of 370), consistent with recent trends of 30.3% on September 10 and 29.2% on September 9. 

In terms of subject matter, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the bulk of the docket with 1,049 cases, posting a 53.7% hearing rate (563 heard)—a sharp recovery from 34.9% on September 10. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) maintained strong efficiency at 59.6% (260 of 436), while Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) experienced a sharp drop in disposal efficiency, converting at just 31.5% (106 of 337) compared to 50.1% yesterday.
